events.title: Fall of Constantinople
events.description: Ottoman forces under Sultan Mehmed II captured Constantinople after a roughly 53-day siege, killing Byzantine Emperor Constantine XI and ending the Byzantine Empire.
events.significance: Marked the end of the Eastern Roman Empire and the Middle Ages for many historians, shifted trade routes between Europe and Asia, and established Ottoman dominance in the eastern Mediterranean.

events.title: Restoration of Charles II
events.description: On his 30th birthday, Charles II entered London to be restored as King of England, Scotland, and Ireland, ending the Interregnum that followed the English Civil War and the execution of Charles I.
events.significance: Restored the monarchy after the Commonwealth and Protectorate period, reshaping the balance between crown and Parliament in Britain.

events.title: Birth of John F. Kennedy
events.description: John Fitzgerald Kennedy, the 35th President of the United States, was born in Brookline, Massachusetts.
events.significance: Kennedy became the youngest person elected U.S. president, led during the Cuban Missile Crisis, and championed the space program and civil rights legislation before his assassination in 1963.

events.title: Eddington Observes Solar Eclipse Confirming General Relativity
events.description: During a total solar eclipse, Arthur Eddington and his team photographed stars near the Sun, measuring the bending of starlight as predicted by Einstein's general theory of relativity.
events.significance: The results, announced later that year, made Albert Einstein world famous and provided key early evidence for general relativity, transforming modern physics.

events.title: First Ascent of Mount Everest
events.description: Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Tenzing Norgay, a Sherpa of Nepal, reached the summit of Mount Everest, the world's highest peak, as part of a British expedition led by John Hunt.
events.significance: Represented a landmark in human exploration and mountaineering, and made Hillary and Tenzing international icons.
